title: SWSI Housing Callout Explorer
description: Line drawing of a single width, single inlet centrifugal fan housing with ten callouts. Explore mode opens a one-sentence description of each part's job; quiz mode hides the labels and shows the ten descriptions in shuffled order, one attempt each, then reports the first-attempt score against a mastery level of 8 of 10. Based on FanPedia p. 60, not to scale.

educational.audience: Adult professional development: new application engineers, sales staff, representatives and facilities staff
educational.topic: Parts of a single width, single inlet (SWSI) centrifugal fan housing
learningObjectives: The learner will identify ten labeled parts of a single width, single inlet centrifugal fan housing from a one-sentence description of each part's job.

accessibility.notes: Every part is a focusable role=button; Tab walks the parts in the callout order (Housing Side to Pedestal), Enter or Space selects one, and after an answer focus moves to Next, so Enter goes on. Verdicts and prompts are announced through FP.announce (aria-live). ✓/✗ glyphs, solid/dashed borders and an "Answer" badge pair with colour. During the quiz part names are hidden from screen readers too until revealed. When the drawing is narrower than about 650 px the callouts switch to numbers with a key list, so callout text stays at 12 px or more.

rules: Explore mode: clicking a callout shows its description; any number of clicks; never scored.
Quiz mode: the 10 descriptions appear once each in shuffled order; one attempt each; a click on the matching part is correct.
Clicking a non-callout area does nothing and uses no attempt.
The correct part is revealed after each answer; a running count 'Correct: n of 10' is shown.
Mastery is 8 of 10 correct on the first attempt; Start over reshuffles.
assumptions: The drawing is a simplified cabinet-oblique line drawing with the inlet funnel, inlet collar and inlet flange pulled off along the shaft line.
limitations: Not to scale and not a specific Twin City Fan model. Rubbing bars (spark-resistant fans only) are left out; Chapter 20 covers them.

sources: FanPedia p. 60 (Centrifugal Fans SWSI): part names and positions
FanPedia p. 59: cutoff and wiper bar function
FanPedia pp. 59 and 185: housing, framing and structural support role
Chapter 7, section 'The Scroll Housing': scroll and cutoff tongue descriptions (standard fan engineering)

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Explore labeled callouts first, then retrieval practice: name each part from its job with the labels hidden, with immediate correction.
keyQuestions: Which part separates air leaving through the outlet from air that would keep circling?
Which inlet part mounts to the inlet opening, which shapes the air, and which bolts to the duct?
commonMisconceptions: The cutoff and the wiper bar are the same piece in the same place.
The side plate and the scroll are one continuous part.
The inlet collar and the inlet funnel are interchangeable names.
assessmentOpportunities: First-attempt score shown as 'First-attempt score: n of 10'; mastery is 8 of 10 on the first attempt.
